Lease Modification Alternatives
Approval of the leases might be conditioned on limiting the area to be leased, limiting approval to one lease, or on alteration of the lease terms. The studies made in connection with this statement indicate that the environmental impacts of coal mining throughout the leased area are substantially the same and that the severity of the impacts of mining is related more to the rate or scale of mining rather than the location within the leased area. Therefore there exist no specific areas for evaluation concerning the limiting of the area to be leased.

Alteration of Lease Terms - Lease terms might be modified to stipulate the type of allowable development, reclamation procedures and/or economic factors.
The present leases, as renegotiated, provide that the lessee may not sell or provide the coal from the leased tracts to any conversion facility on or within 50 miles of the reservation without the approval of the Crow Tribe. Therefore, without further approvals, the coal will have to be mined and shipped out of the area for usage. In the event future approvals for energy conversion facilities are given by the Crow Tribe and the Secretary of the Interior then the environmental impacts as described in Chapter III under Energy Conversion could occur.
Both the Department of Interior and the State of Montana are exercising jurisdiction over mining on the ceded lands; as a result reclamation plans are designed to comply with existing Federal and State laws and regulations and to the terms of the lease.
